PSYC C1000 - Introduction to Psychology (3.0)
    Credit (Degree Applicable)
    Hours: Lecture - 52.5
    Grading: Letter or Pass/No Pass
    Recommended Prep: Readiness for college-level English or ESL 188
    This course is an introduction to psychology, which is the study of the mind and behavior. Students focus on theories and concepts of biological, cognitive, developmental, environmental, social, and cultural influences; their applications; and their research foundations.
    UC Transferable
    Catalog Notes: Formerly PSYC 1
    Course Last Revised: Fall 2025
    PSYC 1B - Biological Psychology (3.0)
    Credit (Degree Applicable)
    Hours: Lecture - 52.5
    Grading: Letter or Pass/No Pass
    Prerequisite: PSYC C1000
    This course examines the biological basis of behavior and mental processes. Psychopharmacology, cognitive neuroscience, research processes, and ethics will also be addressed.
    UC Transferable
    Course Last Revised: Fall 2025
    PSYC 2 - Research Methods (3.0)
    Credit (Degree Applicable)
    Hours: Lecture - 52.5
    Grading: Letter or Pass/No Pass
    Prerequisite: PSYC C1000 and (PSYC 5 or LALS 5 or ECON 5 or STAT C1000)
    An introduction to research methods in psychology. This course presents how researchers in psychology use critical analysis, theories, and methods to generate usable information. Emphasis on research design, experimental procedures, instrumentation, qualitative methods, and the analysis, interpretation, and reporting of findings. Special focus is given to conducting research that is inclusive, culturally informed, and mindful of diverse perspectives.
    UC Transferable
    Catalog Notes: Primarily for psychology majors, related majors, and students interested in the scientific method.
    Course Last Revised: Spring 2026
